doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Meeting Bill Watrous in Colorado Springs
summary: He is nervous meeting Watrous but the two get along after being paired on stage.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Oh my God yeah. Bill and I got along good. First time I ever met him I was scared to death.

They scheduled me and him to do a tune, two tunes together with a rhythm section at this Colorado Springs. And the guy that booked that was famous for that, putting you on the spot you know. Because he did that to me with Carl, with Watrous and — I never played with Rossolino — but anyway he did that so Watrous, he gets up on the stand and I said, “Bill, what a pleasure man, I’ve enjoyed your work for years.” And he said, “Well I caught you on the last set,” he said, “you sounded good.” He said, “Let’s play some music.” Which is neat. And I had to say this, I looked over and I said, “Well, don’t be too mean to me man or I’ll get my kid after you.” Because John at that point, he’d been on the road with Woody, you know, he was on his way up. And Watrous laughed his butt off. And we were great from then on. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
